title: Viewing a One-Room with a Real Estate Agent
situation: You found a 원룸 listing online and meet a 부동산 agent to view a monthly-rent (월세) studio in person.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 인터넷에서 보고 연락드렸는데요, 그 원룸 보러 왔어요.
lines.en: Hello. I called after seeing it online — I came to view that one-room.
lines.note: 보고 연락드렸는데요 = a polite, natural way to say 'I contacted you after seeing it'; 드리다 humbles the verb

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 아, 네. 바로 올라가서 보실까요? 4층이에요.
lines.en: Ah, yes. Shall we go right up and take a look? It's on the 4th floor.
lines.note: 보실까요 = 'shall we look?'; -(으)ㄹ까요 suggests doing something together

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 보증금하고 월세가 어떻게 돼요?
lines.en: What are the deposit and the monthly rent?
lines.note: 어떻게 돼요 = the standard way to ask 'what is it / how much is it' for set figures

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 보증금 천만 원에 월세 오십이에요. 관리비는 따로 칠만 원이고요.
lines.en: It's a ten-million-won deposit with 500,000 a month. The maintenance fee is 70,000 separately.
lines.note: 보증금 천에 월세 오십 = how Koreans say rent: deposit 'X' with monthly 'Y'; 만 원 is dropped in speech

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 관리비에 뭐가 포함돼요? 수도세도 들어가요?
lines.en: What's included in the maintenance fee? Is water included too?
lines.note: 포함되다 = to be included; 수도세 = water bill

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 수도세랑 인터넷은 포함이고, 전기세랑 가스비는 따로 내셔야 돼요.
lines.en: Water and internet are included, but you have to pay electricity and gas separately.
lines.note: -셔야 돼요 = honorific of -아/어야 돼요 (have to); 따로 = separately

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 옵션은 뭐가 있어요? 세탁기랑 에어컨 있어요?
lines.en: What options does it come with? Is there a washing machine and air conditioner?
lines.note: 옵션 = built-in appliances/furnishings that come with the unit

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 풀옵션이에요. 냉장고, 세탁기, 에어컨, 인덕션 다 있어요.
lines.en: It's fully furnished. Fridge, washing machine, AC, and an induction stove — it has everything.
lines.note: 풀옵션 = 'full option', the common term for a fully equipped studio

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 방이 좀 어두운 것 같은데, 햇빛은 잘 들어와요?
lines.en: The room seems a bit dark — does it get good sunlight?
lines.note: 햇빛이 들어오다 = (sun)light comes in; 채광 is the noun for natural lighting

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 남향이라서 낮에는 햇빛 잘 들어와요. 곰팡이 걱정은 없으실 거예요.
lines.en: It faces south, so it gets good light during the day. You won't have to worry about mold.
lines.note: 남향 = south-facing, a big selling point; 곰팡이 = mold, a real concern in cheap 원룸

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 마음에 들어요. 다음 달 초에 입주 가능해요?
lines.en: I like it. Can I move in early next month?
lines.note: 입주 = moving in; 다음 달 초 = early next month

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 네, 가능해요. 계약하시려면 가계약금 먼저 넣으시면 돼요.
lines.en: Yes, that's possible. If you want to sign, you just put down a holding deposit first.
lines.note: 가계약금 = a small holding deposit to reserve the unit before the full contract

tip: Rent is quoted as '보증금 / 월세' (deposit / monthly), and 관리비 (maintenance fee) is almost always extra — always ask what it covers. Check 옵션 (appliances), 채광/방향 (light & direction), and look for 곰팡이 (mold). Never wire a 가계약금 until you've confirmed the listed owner matches the property register (등기부등본).

title: Calling the Landlord About a Broken Boiler and Leak
situation: Your hot water stopped working and there's a water leak under the sink, so you call your 집주인 to ask for repairs.

lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.ko: 여보세요, 사장님. 402호 세입자인데요.
lines.en: Hello, sir. This is the tenant in unit 402.
lines.note: 사장님 = a common, respectful way tenants address a landlord; 여보세요 = 'hello' on the phone

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.ko: 네, 무슨 일 있으세요?
lines.en: Yes, is something the matter?
lines.note: 무슨 일 있으세요 = 'is something wrong?', a natural phone opener

lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.ko: 어제부터 보일러가 고장 나서 따뜻한 물이 안 나와요.
lines.en: The boiler has been broken since yesterday, so no hot water comes out.
lines.note: 고장 나다 = to break down; 어제부터 ... 안 나와요 = '(it) hasn't come out since yesterday'

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.ko: 아이고, 추운데. 온수만 안 나와요, 아니면 난방도 안 돼요?
lines.en: Oh no, and it's cold out. Is it only the hot water, or is the heating out too?
lines.note: 온수 = hot water (formal); 난방 = heating — boilers in Korea handle both

lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.ko: 난방도 안 돼요. 그리고 싱크대 밑에서 물이 새요.
lines.en: The heating is out too. And water is leaking under the sink.
lines.note: 물이 새다 = to leak; 싱크대 밑 = under the sink

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.ko: 누수까지요? 바닥에 물 많이 고였어요?
lines.en: A leak on top of that? Has a lot of water pooled on the floor?
lines.note: 누수 = water leakage (the noun you'll see on repair bills); 물이 고이다 = water pools up

lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.ko: 네, 수건으로 막아 놨는데 계속 새요. 빨리 좀 고쳐 주셨으면 좋겠어요.
lines.en: Yes, I blocked it with a towel but it keeps leaking. I'd really appreciate it if you could fix it soon.
lines.note: 고쳐 주셨으면 좋겠어요 = a polite, indirect request: 'I'd be grateful if you'd fix it'

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 오늘 바로 기사님 보낼게요. 몇 시에 집에 계세요?
lines.en: Understood. I'll send a technician right away today. What time will you be home?
lines.note: 기사님 = repair technician (honorific); 보낼게요 = 'I'll send', the landlord's promise

lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.ko: 저녁 7시 이후에 집에 있어요. 그 전엔 회사라서요.
lines.en: I'm home after 7 p.m. Before that I'm at work.
lines.note: -라서요 = trailing 'because...', softens the reason

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.ko: 그럼 7시 반쯤 기사님이 연락드릴 거예요. 수리비는 제가 낼게요.
lines.en: Then the technician will contact you around 7:30. I'll cover the repair cost.
lines.note: 수리비 = repair fee; landlords pay for repairs to fixtures like the boiler

lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.ko: 감사합니다. 혹시 못 고치면 보일러 교체도 가능할까요?
lines.en: Thank you. If it can't be fixed, would replacing the boiler be possible too?
lines.note: 교체 = replacement; -(으)ㄹ까요 here softly checks possibility

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.ko: 기사님이 보고 판단할 거예요. 너무 걱정 마세요.
lines.en: The technician will decide after looking. Don't worry too much.
lines.note: 걱정 마세요 = 'don't worry', a reassuring set phrase

tip: Repairs to fixed installations — 보일러 (boiler), 누수 (leaks), 변기 (toilet) — are normally the landlord's (집주인) responsibility, so report them fast by phone. Take photos and a quick video as evidence, and confirm who pays (수리비) before the 기사님 (technician) arrives. Address your landlord as 사장님 or 사모님 to keep it polite.
